title: Detecting Axion-Like Particles With Coiled Optical Fibers I: Silica Fibers
authors: Gia Dvali, Sebastian Zell, Tongxuan Zhang
abstract: We propose a new approach to axion-like particle (ALP) searches based on long, coiled optical fibers in an external magnetic field. We develop the theoretical framework required to describe photon-ALP conversion in this geometry by incorporating transverse boundary conditions and fiber bending. For solid silica fibers with refractive index considerably larger than unity, we show that the leading signal is a phase shift of the photon, with negligible loss due to ALP production. This setup has the potential to set new constraints in the regime of large ALP mass. We further identify parameter regions in which boundary effects become important, in particular for hollow-core fibers, where signals due to ALPs can be significantly enhanced.
summary: This paper details a theoretical proposal for detecting Axion-Like Particles (ALPs) using long, coiled optical fibers placed in a magnetic field. By developing a framework that accounts for boundary effects in the fiber, the authors show that the most promising observable is the phase shift of the photon. This technique offers a pathway to constrain ALP properties, especially for larger ALP masses, complementing existing astrophysical searches.
main_problem: The paper proposes a novel method to search for Axion-Like Particles (ALPs) by exploiting photon-ALP conversion within long, coiled optical fibers subjected to an external magnetic field.
main_result: For solid silica fibers, the primary detectable signal is a phase shift of the photon, allowing for setting new constraints on the ALP coupling constant, particularly for large ALP masses.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework incorporating transverse boundary conditions and fiber bending to model the photon-ALP mixing, solving coupled differential equations derived from the interaction Lagrangian.
model_or_system: The system involves the interaction between photons and ALPs ($\mathcal{L}_{	ext{int}} = -g_a E \cdot B$) propagating through an optical fiber. The analysis considers both solid silica fibers (high refractive index) and hollow-core fibers, treating the propagation as a wave mixing problem.
key_observables: Phase shift of the propagating photon ($\delta\phi$), and the general probability of photon-to-ALP conversion.
important_parameters: ALP mass ($m_a$), ALP coupling constant ($g_a$), external magnetic field ($B$), and the refractive index ($n$) of the fiber material.
main_assumptions: Initial analyses use plane-wave approximations, but the full treatment incorporates transverse boundary conditions and bending effects. The sensitivity analysis is particularly strong for large ALP masses.
figures_summary: Figure 1 is an exclusion plot comparing the proposed 'Fiber Bound' sensitivity against existing experimental limits for ALP detection. Figure 2 compares the transverse profiles of the photon and ALP fields in momentum space.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general theoretical description of ALP-photon mixing in a medium (Chunk 2), develops the specific formalism for coiled fibers incorporating boundary effects (Chunk 1), and analyzes the resulting mixing dynamics in different physical regimes (Chunk 3).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it models particle mixing (photon $\leftrightarrow$ ALP) within a structured, confined waveguide (the fiber), requiring the application of boundary conditions to the quantum field equations.
